name: Onion-Skin Pink
lede: Onion-Skin Pink is a warm, muted terracotta pink named for the papery outer skin of a red onion, and it clusters hard around a single decade in our painting archive.

sections.title: The onion's papery coat
sections.body:
The library plots this color on Ridgway's 1912 plate XXVIII, hue 11 double-prime, tone b, and separately records it in Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, plate 11 A 7, first recorded in 1912 [1]. The crowd-sourced xkcd color survey later landed on nearly the same hex under its own name, Pinkish Tan, about 2.1 units away by CIEDE2000 [1]. The name is literal: the thin, dry outer layer of a red or yellow onion's skin, a warm tan-pink rather than the flesh of the bulb [1].

In LCH terms it measures lightness 68, chroma 34, hue 50 degrees, Munsell 1.8YR 6.7/6.3, close to [[vinaceous-cinnamon|Vinaceous-Cinnamon]] and [[light-cinnamon|Light cinnamon]], both nearer to the warm [[cinnamon]] family than to true [[rose|Rose]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 141 of 23,781 paintings, 0.59 percent, as photographed [2]. It is sharply over-represented in the 1910s, in 12 of that decade's 523 paintings, about 3.9 times the expected rate [2]. Amedeo Modigliani is by far its most devoted painter here, carrying it in 4 of his 18 works, 37 times the baseline, well ahead of Lucas Cranach the Elder and Christen Købke [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [2].
